newsitem.title: USA: US attache sees 25.2 Mln T 97/98 Canada wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: US attache sees 25.2 Mln T 97/98 Canada wheat crop.

text.p: Canada will harvest about 25.2 million tonnes of wheat in 1997/98, a sharp drop from the previous year due to lower prices, but still export 20 million tonnes, the U.S. agriculture attache in Ottawa said in a report released Monday.
"Total area seeded to wheat is forecast to dip in 1997" as farmers shifted to canola and other special crops because of more attractive prices, the attache said.
In eastern Canada, winter wheat seedings dropped to 180,000 hectares after problems in 1996 with a wheat blight.
"Due to the drop in area, the initial 1997 wheat production forecast is 25.2 million (metric) tons, down almost 5.3 million tons from last year," the attache wrote.

"Wheat exports are preliminarily forecast to recover to 20 million tons in 1997/98, assuming no repeat of this year's transportation system difficulties. With the anticipated reduction in production, an increase in exports would help draw down ending stocks to 9.1 million tons."

The report projected Canadian wheat exports for 1996/97 at 17.5 million tonnes. It said the Canadian Wheat Board estimated transportation bottlenecks this winter reduced its West Coast exports by two million tonnes. As a result, ending stocks were expected to be 11.7 million tonnes.
